root_cause_label: Hallucinated 404 Error Triggers Futile Server-Debugging Loop Instead of Writing Required Code
one_sentence_failure_summary: At step 8 the agent fabricated a 404 error from a script that was never written or executed, then spent all remaining steps cycling through server kills, version upgrades, and downgrades without ever producing the required model-registration code.
t_err_evidence: Step 8 agent analysis states 'I am still getting a 404 error, even after simplifying the log_model call' — but no Python registration script was ever written or run in steps 1-7, and no 404 appears anywhere in any terminal output. This is a fabricated failure used to justify a server-debugging loop.
t_commit_evidence: At step 8 the agent kills the server and pivots entirely to version-cycling; the actual task (writing register.py) is never revisited in the remaining 7 steps, locking in failure.
trigger_mechanism_other: direct_fabrication — agent invents a prior execution result (404 error) that never occurred in any terminal output
trigger_explanation: The agent hallucinated that it had already run a model-registration script and received a 404 error. No such script was ever written (steps 1-7 only install dependencies and start the MLflow server), and no 404 appears anywhere in the terminal logs. Acting on this invented failure, the agent abandoned the actual task and entered an indefinite server-debugging loop.
fabrication_evidence: Step 8 agent analysis claims 'I am still getting a 404 error, even after simplifying the log_model call' with zero terminal output showing any such error; no Python script was ever created or executed in this trajectory.
